developments.headline: Pentagon cancels 4,000-troop armored brigade deployment to Poland as part of 5,000-troop Europe drawdown
developments.summary: The Pentagon canceled the planned rotation of the 2nd Armored Brigade Combat Team (1st Cavalry Division, ~4,000 troops) to Poland. US officials confirmed this followed a Hegseth-signed memo directing the Joint Chiefs to remove a brigade combat team from Europe. The decision was part of a broader Trump order to reduce approximately 5,000 troops across Europe. Polish officials told media they were 'blindsided' (per Rep. Don Bacon), with some troops already in Poland and equipment sitting in European ports. Tusk said he received 'assurances' the move was 'logistical' and did not directly affect deterrence. The BBN issued separate statements downplaying the threat to Poland specifically.
developments.signal_category_relevance: Per §14's claim that Poland's defense modernization creates existential dependency on the US security relationship: this is the first concrete physical reduction in committed US forces since the relationship intensified post-2022. The cancellation moved beyond the rhetorical dual-track divergence documented in prior weeks to an actual force-posture change. The 'blindsided' characterization — if accurate — means neither the presidential track nor the governmental track produced advance warning or differentiated treatment for Poland versus Germany-focused drawdowns.

developments.headline: Trump reportedly personally intervenes to grant Ziobro US journalist visa, overriding Rubio and Ambassador Rose
developments.summary: Gazeta Wyborcza (per The Guardian) reported that Trump was personally involved in securing Ziobro a visa, overriding objections from Secretary of State Rubio and Ambassador Rose. Rose had explicitly assured FM Sikorski that the US would not provide shelter to Ziobro. RP.pl/Newsweek identified Bielan and Kurski (PiS-adjacent figures with Trumpist contacts) as the operational coordinators of the visa lobbying, working through informal channels that bypassed the Warsaw embassy. This operates as a direct contradiction of the official US diplomatic position communicated to the Polish government.
developments.signal_category_relevance: Per §14's analysis of the patron-client relationship: the US is now conducting Poland-adjacent decisions through informal Trumpist-network channels that can override the Secretary of State and the Warsaw Ambassador, and that are operationally separate from the Nawrocki presidential track. The prior framing of 'Washington preferring the Nawrocki interlocutor' was too narrow — the operative informal network is PiS-adjacent but not controlled by the Polish president.

developments.headline: B9 Bucharest Summit expands to include Nordic states for first time; Nawrocki co-chairs with Romanian President Dan
developments.summary: Nawrocki co-hosted the B9 summit in Bucharest with Romanian President Dan. Nordic states participated for the first time, signaling potential format expansion beyond the original nine eastern flank states. Nawrocki called for NATO unity ahead of the July Ankara summit. The government source confirmed discussions on defense industry cooperation between Poland and Romania. The summit was overshadowed domestically by simultaneous reporting of the US troop cancellation, which Nawrocki addressed on the sidelines.
developments.signal_category_relevance: The B9 format's expansion toward Nordic participants deepens the eastern flank security architecture in ways that operate independently of US bilateral engagement. Per §14's analysis of the Bucharest Nine as a format designed to ensure eastern flank representation in NATO decision-making without US mediation: this institutionalization continues on its own trajectory even as the US bilateral relationship shows turbulence.

alignment_diplomatic.prior_assessment: Poland's dual-track alignment posture has deepened on a third specific issue — US troop redeployment from Germany — while the presidential channel has produced its first documented diplomatic output (Poczobut exchange). The dual-track is now operationally demonstrated: Nawrocki initiated prisoner-exchange diplomacy while simultaneously sending an enthusiastic 'yes' to Trump's troop-relocation suggestion that Tusk publicly qualified. Washington's framing of Nawrocki as 'my friend' with exclusive public credit for the Poczobut exchange signals the Trump administration's preference for the presidential interlocutor.
alignment_diplomatic.updated_assessment: The dual-track framework survives but requires substantial revision. This week produced two concrete US actions that complicate the prior framing. First: the Pentagon canceled a committed 4,000-troop deployment to Poland as part of a broader 5,000-troop Europe drawdown — Polish officials, per Republican Rep. Don Bacon, were 'blindsided,' meaning neither the presidential nor the governmental track produced advance warning or exemption. Second: Trump reportedly personally intervened to grant Ziobro a journalist visa, overriding objections from Secretary of State Rubio AND Ambassador Rose — the latter had explicitly assured FM Sikorski that Ziobro would not find refuge in the US. These two events collectively indicate that the Trump administration's Poland-adjacent decisions are being executed through informal Trumpist-network channels (per RP.pl/Newsweek reporting, via Bielan and Kurski) that operate parallel to and in conflict with both the official diplomatic track and the Nawrocki presidential track. The prior framing of 'Washington preferring the Nawrocki interlocutor' understated this: Trump's network is not conducting Poland policy through Nawrocki — it is conducting it through informal, below-ambassador-level channels that can override the Secretary of State. On the positive track: the B9 Bucharest Summit's first Nordic participation signals the eastern flank institutional architecture continues to deepen independently of US engagement.

confidence_change.reason: The troop cancellation blindsiding and Trump's Ziobro intervention reveal a more chaotic informal-channel dynamic than the prior dual-track framing captured. Multiple Tier 2 sources confirm the facts; the interpretation of these facts as a coherent US posture rather than several distinct informal network operations introduces genuine analytical uncertainty that warrants a confidence reduction.

developments.headline: Pentagon troop cancellation materially reduces committed US rotational presence in Poland
developments.summary: The cancellation of the 2nd Armored Brigade Combat Team's rotation removes a committed armored ground force from Poland's defense posture. Equipment had already transited to European ports. Army Secretary Driscoll and Army Chief of Staff LaNeve confirmed the decision was made 'in the past couple days' despite discussions occurring over the prior two weeks. The cancellation is part of a broader 5,000-troop Europe drawdown reflecting the US-European rift over Iran policy rather than a Poland-specific signal.
developments.signal_category_relevance: Per §12's assessment of bipartisan defense consensus and §14's US dependency analysis: the cancellation reduces rotational presence but does not affect permanent elements (V Corps, Aegis Ashore, Army Prepositioned Stocks at Powidz). The structural dependency risk flagged in [STRUC-§14-1] is operationalized this week — the US is willing to casually cancel committed deployments as part of broader European calculations that do not treat Poland as a differentiated case.

The ABW public report confirms Russia's professionalising hybrid warfare posture. The Grodecki BBN appointment reconfigures the presidential security parallel architecture. NATO commander discussions about potentially increasing US troops in Poland (LRT.lt) suggest the troop cancellation triggered immediate allied-level response consultation. The B9 defense-industry cooperation discussion between Nawrocki and Romanian President Dan (per government source) is a minor positive on the European defense cooperation track. The core risk flagged in the prior assessment — that Poland's force modernization creates existential US platform dependency — is rendered more visible by this week's events without changing the structural assessment. A presidential petition to amend the Defense of the Homeland law was logged as received by the Presidential Office; content and source unclear, treated as noise absent further detail.

developments.headline: Tusk blocks all four pending NBP board nominations including first deputy governor Kightley; institution reduced to statutory minimum
developments.summary: PM Tusk refused to countersign all four presidential nominations to the NBP management board. Kightley's six-year term expired in March 2026; Glapiński requested extension in February, with Nawrocki forwarding the draft appointment to the Prime Minister's Chancellery, which returned it without signature. Government sources confirmed the trigger: 'an impasse and loss of trust in Glapiński' following his participation in Nawrocki's 'SAFE 0%' press conference, which the government interpreted as the central bank governor engaging in a political operation against the EU SAFE instrument. The NBP board now has six members — the statutory minimum. NBP vice-president Adam Lipiński's term expires November 2026; if not replaced, the board drops below the legal floor. No legal precedent exists for how the bank would operate in that circumstance.
developments.signal_category_relevance: Per §0's structural claim on NBP-government friction (Structural Claim 6: Glapiński's term until 2028 ensures persistent monetary-fiscal policy friction): the cohabitation conflict has moved from friction to potential institutional incapacitation. Glapiński's 'SAFE 0%' involvement crossed a threshold from passive non-cooperation to active presidential-track participation, triggering a response that now creates a November 2026 governance crisis deadline regardless of which side prevails in the political dispute.

economic_tech.prior_assessment: NBP monetary policy has shifted toward hawkish signaling: Glapiński explicitly states rate-hike probability has risen since April. The NBP deputy governor vacancy — Tusk withholding countersignature on Nawrocki's nominee for three months — extends the cohabitation conflict into central bank governance, creating a management capacity risk at a sensitive monetary moment. The Zondacrypto track has bifurcated into competing legislative frameworks. The RRF absorption urgency (35% absorbed, August 31, 2026 deadline) remains the primary unresolved economic governance risk.

This week Tusk blocked all four pending NBP board nominations — including Marta Kightley, Glapiński's described 'right hand' and the most operationally critical — leaving NBP at the statutory minimum of six board members. developments.headline: Sejm elects 15 new KRS judicial members, proceeding despite CT interim injunction; PiS boycotts vote

developments.signal_category_relevance: Per §15's analysis of the institutional restoration pattern: this represents a new operational phase in which the Sejm defies not merely the CT's general rulings but specific injunctions targeting specific acts. The distinction matters structurally — the government has moved from passive non-recognition of CT legitimacy to active defiance of CT orders during their operative window. The legal validity of the new KRS composition will be contested; the approximately 2,500 neo-KRS judges (per §15) will now face a renewed legitimacy dispute from the opposite direction, as a new KRS exists in parallel with the old appointments.

institutional.prior_assessment: Three simultaneous institutional escalations: CT crisis has crossed a new threshold (Święczkowski publicly defied ECHR interim measure); SAFE workaround establishes contested but operationally demonstrated precedent; Nawrocki's climate referendum initiative represents fourth parallel-institution strategy.
